title: Alma Comes to Speak
summary: Alma tells the people that this is his first time addressing them in person. He explains that business at the judgment-seat had kept him away, and that another now reigns in his stead.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says this is the first time he has spoken to them by his own mouth.
Alma had been confined to the judgment-seat by much business.
Another has received the judgment-seat to reign in Alma's stead, and the Lord granted Alma's visit.

unspecified_visual_details: Audience size and appearance
Meeting place and architecture

narration.text: I attempt to address you in my language
the judgment-seat hath been given to another

prohibited_inventions: Do not stage the transfer of the judgment-seat; it is reported, not shown.

title: Hopes for the People
summary: Alma says he hoped the people had humbled themselves and remained blameless. He rejoices that the brethren at Zarahemla are again established in righteousness, and expresses trust in his present audience.

explicit_facts.text: Alma hoped the people had humbled themselves before God and continued supplicating for grace.
Alma rejoices that the brethren at Zarahemla are established again in righteousness.
Alma says his joy for the brethren at Zarahemla followed affliction and sorrow.
Alma trusts that his audience is not in unbelief or pride, has not set its heart on riches and worldly vanity, and worships the true and living God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma continues speaking to the audience.
unspecified_visual_details: Audience reactions
Meeting place appearance

narration.text: I have come having great hopes and much desire
blessed be the name of God
I trust that ye are not in a state of so much unbelief

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The brethren at Zarahemla and their earlier afflictions are mentioned retrospectively.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage the brethren at Zarahemla or their afflictions as present events.

title: The Redeemer Will Come
summary: Alma teaches that the Redeemer will come among his people in the not-distant future. He says he does not know whether this will happen during the Redeemer's mortal life.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says the Redeemer will come among his people in a time not far distant.
Alma says he does not know whether the Redeemer will come among them during his mortal dwelling.
Alma affirms that the Lord God has power to do all things according to his word.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma's teaching may be rendered as off-screen speech over the supported speaking setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The Redeemer's appearance
The circumstances of his future coming

narration.text: the time is not far distant that the Redeemer liveth and cometh among his people
Now as to this thing I do not know

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is prophecy, not a narrated appearance of the Redeemer.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Redeemer arriving or assign a manner or time to his coming.

title: Prepare the Way of the Lord
summary: Alma relays the Spirit's instruction to call the people to repentance, prepare the way of the Lord, and walk in his straight paths, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.

explicit_facts.text: The Spirit told Alma to call the people to repent, prepare the Lord's way, and walk in his straight paths.
Alma declares that the kingdom of heaven is at hand and the Son of God comes upon the earth.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma speaks to the audience; the Spirit's instruction is reported, not shown as a visible figure.
unspecified_visual_details: Any literal road or path
The Son of God's appearance

narration.text: Repent ye, and prepare the way of the Lord
the kingdom of heaven is at hand

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The straight paths are figurative instruction.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a supernatural road, the Spirit, or an undescribed appearance of the Son of God.

title: Mary and the Son of God
summary: Alma teaches that the Son of God will be born of Mary at Jerusalem, and that Mary will conceive by the power of the Holy Ghost.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says the Son of God will be born of Mary at Jerusalem.
Mary is described as a virgin and a precious, chosen vessel who will conceive by the power of the Holy Ghost.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma delivers this prophecy as speech, rather than staging the birth.
unspecified_visual_details: Mary's appearance
The circumstances of conception and birth

narration.text: he shall be born of Mary, at Jerusalem

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is prophetic teaching, not a present-tense account of Mary's conception or the birth.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage Mary, the conception, or the birth as present events.

title: The Son of God Will Suffer
summary: Alma teaches that the Son of God will suffer pains, afflictions, temptations, and death, and take upon him the infirmities and sins of his people so he may succor and deliver them.

explicit_facts.text: The Son of God will suffer pains, afflictions, and temptations of every kind.
He will take upon him the pains and sicknesses of his people, death, and their infirmities.
Alma says the Son of God suffers according to the flesh to take upon him the sins of his people and blot out their transgressions.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma's teaching can be presented as off-screen speech over the supported setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The Redeemer's appearance
The manner of suffering, death, or deliverance

that he might take upon him the sins of his people

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage teaches about future suffering; it does not narrate a present suffering scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific injury, execution, or healing event.

title: Repentance and Baptism
summary: Alma calls the people to repent, be born again, lay aside sin, and enter a covenant with God, witnessing their willingness through baptism.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says the people must repent and be born again, and calls them to be baptized unto repentance.
Alma calls them to lay aside sin, covenant to keep God's commandments, and witness it that day by going into baptismal waters.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma addresses the people; the call to enter baptismal waters does not narrate that anyone does so.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Baptism is exhorted, not narrated as an event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a baptism taking place.

title: A Promise to the Faithful
summary: Alma teaches that whoever keeps God's commandments will remember his words and have eternal life according to the testimony of the Holy Spirit.

explicit_facts.text: Alma promises eternal life, according to the Holy Spirit's testimony, to whoever does this and thereafter keeps God's commandments.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma's words continue as off-screen speech over the supported speaking setting.
unspecified_visual_details: Any visible form of eternal life or the Holy Spirit

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The promise is teaching, not a visible supernatural event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict eternal life or the Holy Spirit as a visible event or figure.

title: Alma Rejoices in Their Faith
summary: Alma asks whether the people believe, says he knows they do through the Spirit's manifestation in him, and rejoices that his hopes for them have been fulfilled.

explicit_facts.text: Alma asks whether the people believe and says he knows they believe by the Spirit's manifestation in him.
Alma says his desire that they not be in the dilemma of their brethren has been fulfilled.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma continues speaking to the people.

title: The Paths of Righteousness
summary: Alma says the people are in the paths of righteousness and making the Lord's paths straight. He teaches that God does not walk in crooked paths or turn from what he has said.

explicit_facts.text: Alma perceives that the people are in the paths of righteousness and the path leading to God's kingdom.
Alma teaches that God does not walk in crooked paths or turn from what he has said.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma's teaching may be presented as off-screen speech over the supported setting.
unspecified_visual_details: Any literal path or visual symbol for God's course

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The paths and eternal round are figurative teachings.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict supernatural roads or a literal eternal loop.

title: Walking Blamelessly
summary: Alma teaches that nothing unclean can be received into God's kingdom and says he has spoken to awaken the people to their duty to God.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says God does not dwell in unholy temples and that nothing unclean can be received into God's kingdom.
Alma says he has spoken to awaken the people to their duty to God and to walk blamelessly.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma continues his address; the kingdom and uncleanliness are subjects of teaching, not depicted events.
unspecified_visual_details: Any temple or visible form of God's kingdom

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These statements are doctrinal instruction, not a description of a visible setting.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an unholy temple or judgment scene.

title: Counsel in Righteous Living
summary: Alma counsels humility, gentleness, patience, temperance, diligence, asking for needs, and gratitude. He also counsels faith, hope, and charity, with an abundance of good works.

explicit_facts.text: Alma counsels humility, submissiveness, gentleness, patience, long-suffering, temperance, diligence, asking for needs, and gratitude.
Alma counsels faith, hope, and charity, and says the people will abound in good works.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma's counsel can be presented as off-screen speech without staging examples of conduct.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The virtues are counsel, not separate narrated actions.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent specific good works or a prayer scene.

title: Alma's Closing Blessing
summary: Alma blesses the people and speaks of their being brought to the kingdom of heaven. He rejoices over their diligence and invokes peace upon them and their households, lands, flocks, herds, and possessions.

explicit_facts.text: Alma blesses the people and speaks of their being brought to sit with Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and the holy prophets in the kingdom of heaven.
Alma rejoices over the diligence and heed the people gave to his word.
Alma invokes God's peace upon the people, their houses, lands, flocks, herds, and possessions.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma concludes his address before the audience.
